The definitions the refuted statement is built from (IsAnalyticModelFamily, XAChart, IsXAManifold, IsTamifyingTopology, IsVirtuallyTame, IsLocallyGaloisian, HasAutContinuousTamifying) are byte-identical to the pre-WP-43g copy, and GX's IsLocallyUnloopable and SingularGXStructure are strict-library notions. None of the removed or changed names is used in code in any other file: the BTZ/*.lean and SpreadTop.lean hits are comments, as REPORT says. REFUTATION FIDELITY: LocalVirtTameStatement is the paper's l.1974 statement over Type: an analytic family, models locally Galoisian (the literal DEC-55 IsSLSCInCC over every open), each model with a tamifying topology on which every a.e. automorphism of X̃_α is continuous (DEC-87 (b)), models T2/LPC/first countable/connected (DEC-66 (a), l.1712), and (i) quantified over IsXAManifold. IsXAManifold is the DEC-67 (e) notion, which is stronger than the printed IsXAManifoldPrinted, so the failure of (i) also refutes the printed reading. (ii) holds by hasAutContinuousTamifying_XA.isVirtuallyTame, and (i) fails at VV. One standing hypothesis is missing from the refuted statement: X connected (l.341, DEC-39), see the major issue. LPC of X is covered, because IsLocallyUnloopable carries LocPathConnectedSpace. The counterexample satisfies the missing hypothesis: `instance : ConnectedSpace XS` at l.6174. I typechecked a strengthened refutation via stdin (adding [ConnectedSpace X] [LocPathConnectedSpace X], plus SecondCountableTopology on the models and on the quantified N, which are inferred for the subtypes of ℂ²) with the same three-line proof term, and it closes. Local Galoisianity at s holds under the literal DEC-55 notion, because the loops are based at s through reg and contract radially in Ω(s,s,reg). That is the paper's definition, so it is not an abuse. The model geometry X is not a manifold at 0. This is allowed by l.341/l.1650 and is disclosed and asked of the author. issues.where: GX.LocalVirtTameStatement (Models.lean l.8508–8519), hence GX.not_localVirtTameStatement (l.8521) and the REPORT/docstring claim 'theo:local_virt_tame is FALSE as printed'; also GX.ThinCex.local_virt_tame_counterexample (l.8482) and REPORT theo:local_virt_tame hypotheses[4]
issues.problem: For a refutation, the strength flips: the refuted Lean statement must carry at least the paper's hypotheses, or its negation is weaker than 'the paper's theorem is false'. LocalVirtTameStatement's binders on X are ContinuousConstSMul, LocallyConnectedSpace, T2Space, IsRigidAction and FaithfulSMul, with IsLocallyUnloopable as an explicit hypothesis. It OMITS [ConnectedSpace X], which belongs to the paper's analytical structure (l.341: 'a connected, locally connected, Hausdorff topological space X …', ruled as the definition by DEC-39) and is the standing assumption of §2.5 (l.1660). Its docstring says 'over a locally unloopable analytic structure', which reads as DEC-39's notion, connected included. So the certifying declaration refutes a statement with fewer hypotheses than the paper's. The counterexample does satisfy it (instance ConnectedSpace XS, l.6174), so the mathematics is right. But neither not_localVirtTameStatement nor the conjunction local_virt_tame_counterexample records it, and REPORT's list of hypotheses verified for the counterexample omits it. This is an unreported weakening of the certified negation.
issues.fix: Add `[ConnectedSpace X]` to the X binders of LocalVirtTameStatement (optionally also `[LocPathConnectedSpace X]` for DEC-39's 'loc. path-conn. where used', which is redundant with IsLocallyUnloopable). The proof of not_localVirtTameStatement is unchanged: I checked a strengthened variant through `lake env lean --stdin` with [ConnectedSpace X] [LocPathConnectedSpace X], SecondCountableTopology on the models and on N, and the same term `hnV ((h … hX hfam hgal htam).2 hii _ hV)` typechecks. Mention X connected in local_virt_tame_counterexample's docstring and in REPORT's hypothesis note.
